---
title: "Fleet CI"
description: "Run the CI-equivalent check set for one commit, sharded across trusted development machines over SSH."
updatedAt: "2026-11-19"

## What it runs

`bun fleet:ci` checks one exact commit on several machines at once. Each shard
mirrors the command a GitHub workflow runs for the same check:

| Shard | Workflow | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type-check` | `type-check.yaml` | Builds workspace packages; never on the local host |
| `unit-0` to `unit-3` | `turbo-unit-tests.yaml` | Same planner as CI shards; Web suites get a disposable Redis |
| `root-scripts-0` to `root-scripts-2` | `turbo-unit-tests.yaml` | The complete root suite, split with `--test-shard` |
| `oxlint`, `oxfmt` | `oxc-check.yaml` | Workspace binaries at the workflow's pinned versions |
| `i18n` | `i18n-check.yaml` | Sort, translation, key parity and namespace checks |
| `docs-seo` | `docs-seo-check.yaml` | Inventory, SEO assets and docs audit |
| `codex-plugin` | `codex-plugin.yaml` | Plugin and docs navigation validation |

App builds, E2E, CodeQL and deploy workflows stay in GitHub Actions.

## Usage

```bash
bun fleet:ci --plan                    # admission and placement only
bun fleet:ci                           # HEAD on every admitted host
bun fleet:ci --sha origin/main         # an exact pushed commit
bun fleet:ci --only 'root-scripts-*,oxlint' --hosts build-box
bun fleet:ci --sweep                   # after an interrupted run
```

Logs land in `$TMPDIR/fleet-ci-<sha>/<shard>.log` (or `--out`). The summary
prints each shard's host, status and minutes, followed by the last lines of
every failed shard. The exit code is non-zero when any shard fails, times out
or cannot be placed.

## Hosts and admission

Machine-specific hosts live outside the repository, in the JSON array named by
`$FLEET_CI_HOSTS` or `~/.tuturuuu/fleet-ci/hosts.json`:

```json
[
  {
    "id": "build-box",
    "ssh": "build-box",
    "repo": "/srv/checkouts/tuturuuu",
    "slots": 4,
    "builds": true,
    "minFreeGiB": 60
  }
]
```

The checkout running the command is always added as `local` (one slot,
`builds: false`, 24 GiB floor) unless the file defines `local`. The production
server and each of its aliases are refused before any connection, including
when listed in the file.

Before scheduling, each host is probed over SSH:

- free space on the repository volume must meet the host's `minFreeGiB`, which
  stays at or above that host's own `ttr resources` heavy-admission floor;
- Node must be 24, the CI version. The probe prefers `~/tools/pinned-24.*`,
  then nvm or Homebrew `node@24`;
- slots shrink when the host is already loaded;
- shards that need Redis go only to hosts with `redis-server` or a running
  Docker daemon.

A host with `builds: false` only receives light shards, so app and package
builds never run on the machine you are working on.
Hosts that run `ttr resources` execute install and every shard through their
own queue; a refused admission (exit 75) requeues the shard on another host.
When a host's shims need a pinned runtime, set `ttrRuntime` for that host.

## Lifecycle

1. Resolve the commit. A commit that is not on `origin` travels as a Git
   bundle containing only the commits after `origin/main`.
2. On each admitted host: `git worktree add --detach` under
   `<repo>/.worktrees/fleet-ci-<sha>-<pid>`, then `bun install --frozen-lockfile`.
3. Shards are pulled heaviest first. A shared setup step, such as the
   workspace package build, runs once per host before the first shard that
   needs it.
4. Cleanup always runs: it stops leftover shard processes, removes the
   worktree, prunes worktree metadata and deletes the bundle. If the controller
   is killed, run `bun fleet:ci --sweep`; it removes every `fleet-ci-*`
   worktree, so never run it while another fleet run is active.

## Interpreting results

macOS hosts can differ from the Linux CI runners. A failure that depends on
process-group signals, filesystem case or timing should be confirmed on a CI
runner before treating it as a regression. Record confirmed flakes and timing
evidence in the development-tooling skill's `references/ci-learnings.md`.

## Fleet status webhook Worker

The Worker stores a bounded projection of signed GitHub Actions, check-suite,
pull request, and push deliveries. Set the repository allowlist explicitly.
The Worker starts disabled in configuration, and the Durable Object starts
stopped. The operator start endpoint enables stored work only when the
configuration flag is also enabled. An authenticated
`POST /v1/control/stop` persists the stop before acknowledging it. An admitted
fallback can finish before stop is acknowledged. The stopped object rejects
reads and ingest and starts no fallback, including after a runtime restart.

Use independent secrets named `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`,
`FLEET_STATUS_READ_TOKEN`, and `FLEET_STATUS_OPERATOR_TOKEN`. The reader token
grants access to all configured repositories, so only issue it to fleet
principals authorized for that set. The optional
`FLEET_STATUS_GITHUB_TOKEN` needs only repository Actions read permission.
It is sent solely to GitHub from the Worker. Clients receive private,
non-cacheable projections without raw webhook payloads or credentials.
GitHub's HMAC authenticates the original bytes before payload parsing.

The status API reads `/v1/repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/status`.
Pull request projections use `/v1/repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>`.
Coverage is complete only for a recent complete GitHub snapshot. Webhook-only
projections can be partial and do not establish a terminal CI gate.

| Path | Operation bound |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid webhook signature or body larger than 1 MiB | No Durable Object request or write |
| Accepted signed event | One Durable Object request and one state write, with at most 3,600 accepted events per repository per UTC hour |
| Duplicate delivery or older event | One Durable Object request and zero state writes |
| Status without reconciliation | One Durable Object request and zero state writes |
| Fallback reconciliation | One GitHub request, no retries, a four-second deadline, and at most two state writes |
| Fallback across the allowlist | One request per repository per 60 seconds, capped at eight repositories, or 480 requests per rolling hour |
| Stopped object | Zero upstream requests and zero event or budget writes |

The Durable Object reserves a reconciliation slot before the upstream request,
so failed responses and restarts consume the slot. It retains at most 96 event
projections, 256 delivery IDs and one reconciliation snapshot per configured
repository. It schedules no background jobs. The bounds count application
operations. Hosted provider billing and throughput require deployed telemetry.

Run isolated checks from the repository root with the host resource broker.

```sh
ttr resources run -- bun --cwd apps/fleet-status test
ttr resources run -- bun --cwd apps/fleet-status verify:runtime
```

The fixture tests assert zero Durable Object requests for invalid ingress,
one ingest write for repeated deliveries, one upstream request for distinct
SHAs sharing a repository cooldown, and no additional upstream work after
stop. The Workerd check uses disposable secrets and SQLite persistence and
exercises six concurrent copies of the same delivery and the stop fence across
a runtime restart. Its fallback transport is disabled.
